## Natural history notes

A native evergreen tree in the laurel family, characterized by glossy, aromatic leaves with pale bluish-green undersides, reddish-brown furrowed bark, and small dark blue to black fruits. Redbay occurs throughout Florida in xeric to mesic woodlands, scrub, hammocks, and other upland habitats, although it can tolerate a wide range of soil moisture conditions. Its fruits are eaten by birds and mammals, while its foliage serves as a host for several insects. Redbay populations have declined substantially in parts of Florida because of laurel wilt disease, which is spread by the non-native redbay ambrosia beetle. The species is also widely treated under the accepted name Persea borbonia, with Tamala borbonia used as a synonym.
